_comment: Nightly full-scope mutation scope (W1-T133, MASTER-PLAN §5/D-10). `mutate` mirrors stryker.conf.json's own `mutate` key syntax (a flat glob array; a `!`-prefixed entry is an exclusion) but widened to the WHOLE src/** tree instead of the PR gate's single classify.ts target -- this is what lets the nightly workflow own the global mutation score while stryker.conf.json (untouched by this task) keeps the PR gate diff-scoped. `!src/**/*.test.ts` is belt-and-suspenders: test/** already sits outside src/** so it can never match this glob anyway, and scripts/mutation-ratchet.mjs's resolveMutateScope() ALSO hard-excludes `test/**` unconditionally regardless of what this file says -- a test file is never a mutation target in either scope, enforced twice. `fileCap` bounds how many of the matched files any SINGLE nightly run mutates (the ~4-hour full-tree run this task exists to keep off the PR path); scripts/mutation-ratchet.mjs's `--nightly-plan` mode deterministically samples down to this cap, keyed on the day-of-year, so the sample ROTATES and the whole matched set is visited once every ceil(matched-file-count / fileCap) nights -- never a silent partial-coverage-forever.
_commandBudgetComment: A COST CEILING, not a detector -- nothing here judges a file, it decides only what fits in a night. With Stryker's command runner a mutated file costs `mutants x command-wall-clock / concurrency`, so the command's wall clock IS the cost. `--nightly-plan` runs each candidate's own test command once, killed at this budget, and EXCLUDES (by name, never silently) any candidate that overruns it. It measures rather than counting importers because MEASURED on this tree importer count barely predicts command time -- real sets of 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 11 importers timed at 15.6s, 1.3s, 16.4s, 2.8s, 19.2s, 16.9s and 6.4s, since `node --test` runs files concurrently and the slowest file dominates. 8000 comes from the arithmetic and from a measured sweep of ALL 109 modules' own commands: median 3,475ms, p75 16,714ms, and 13 modules (every hot one -- plan.ts, run-task.ts, status.ts, review.ts, worker.ts, serve.ts, trace.ts, panel-actions.ts and the rest) still running at 40s. At 8000ms, 67 of the 109 modules are eligible (61%); at 20000ms it would be 81 (74%) but a worst-case night triples. Worst case per night is fileCap x commandBudgetMs of planning (~2 min) plus fileCap x mutants x budget / concurrency of mutation; against the three real per-file runs measured for this change (22, 47 and 74 mutants in 14s, 10s and 18s), a typical night lands near half an hour. RAISE IT to cover more of the tree at the cost of a longer night; LOWER IT for a faster one. Whatever it is set to, the excluded files are named in the job log and in the failure issue, so what the nightly did not measure is never hidden.
